section: Proposition H - Parcel Tax to Fund Public Muni Operations
text: Prop H would introduce a parcel tax from 2027-2042 to assist in funding San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency operations. The anticipated revenue generated from this tax would be about $177 million. The Chamber supports Prop H as public transit is a critical driver of the San Francisco economy, helping workers, residents, and businesses stay connected.

section: Mayor Lurie Joined by Firefighters and Police Officers in Strong Opposition to Proposition I
text: The timing of the special-interest led Proposition I could not be worse. San Francisco is in the middle of its most aggressive first-responder hiring push in years.

section: Quoted words of SFPOA President Louis Wong
text: "We are finally turning the corner on staffing after years of losing officers, and this is exactly the wrong moment to drain the fund that's paying for that comeback," said Louis Wong, President of the San Francisco Police Officers Association.

section: Proposition J, Foreclosure Transfer Tax: NO
text: San Francisco's commercial real estate market is already under tremendous stress, and adding transfer taxes to foreclosures and distressed property workouts would make matters worse. The city should be encouraging capital to return to its struggling real estate market, not making it more expensive to invest.
